description.narrative: Detta är ett 3 årigt entreprenörskapsprogram för ungdomar som ska genomföras av CARE och rikta sig till 18 000 ungdomar. Programmet kommer att pågå under perioden september 2013 till september 2016.
This is a 3 year youth entrepreneurship programme to be implemented by CARE targeting 18 000 youths. The programme will be during the period September 2013 to September 2016

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2016Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The project managed to reach 19,077 youths for either entrepreneurship or technical skills training. According to an End of Project Evaluation Report, over the life of the project their average incomes increased from $1,530 to $1,693 against the backdrop of a declining economy and a poor agricultural season (this was a mainly rural focused intervention with an agro-based economy).
Post training, 65% of the trained youth established new businesses and 70% expanded or diversified their business (this figure includes newly formed and old businesses which went on to expend or diversify). There was over 80% participation in some sort of business or social network by the youths which strengthened their resilience to economic and other challenges. The greatest improvement of 30% in young women's economic control/decision was on small livestock (poultry etc); there was only a marginal improvement (7%) in cattle - meaning it still remains a men's domain.
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) still struggle to formalise their businesses and their operations - 52%'s business operations were still disengaged from formal structures and regulators, 88% are not formally registered, and only 27% accessed some kind of loan from formal financial institutions. Though the access to formal finance was an improvement from 10% at baseline, it was still very low - mainly due to that financial institutions only deal with formally registered businesses. However evidently most MSMEs can not afford the cost of compliance with regulatory requirements and hence find value in staying informal.
Loan repayment rates still remain very good - despite that businesses were mostly agro-based and the loans were made in the last year of the project, when the agricultural season which experienced a drought and a currency crisis. Young women faired better in repaying their loans - 82%, compared to young men's 63%; dragging the overall loan repayment rate to 79%.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
